3e22b8bd6cbd: He stayed in the town, and he became his own master. After years as a salesman — with Esbjerg Cykellager and with Nellemann in Aarhus — on 1 October 1961 he bought the mineral-water factory <t1>Tropil</t1> from its founder, Villy Bratborg. Production had by then fallen to around 300,000 bottles a year. Silkjær began by having the soft drinks analysed in a laboratory and made a new recipe; some of the old customers did not care for it, but sales rose. On 1 October 1964 he moved the factory to a new building at Randersvej 8, and in the years 1965—67 he was up to around a million bottles a year with ten to twelve employees.
af3d49a13da3: Then the times turned. The customers were still mostly private households, but women had gone out to work, and a factory that sold to homes could only reach them in the evenings and on Saturday afternoons. Carrying on would have demanded fully automatic machines and an entirely different operation. Together with serious illness in the family, it took the heart out of him. On <t1>24 February 1969</t1> he closed Tropil. His wife, <t2>Karen Marie</t2>, née Schmidt, born on 9 September 1917 — a month before him — died four years later, on 12 January 1973, and was buried in Fourfeldt Cemetery.<t3>?</t3><n1/> The machines went to Ceres in Aarhus, the stock to Saltum Brewery, the building to a furnishing company — and Tage Ewald Silkjær went back to his old trade as a commission salesman. He died on 2 January 1995, seventy-seven years old. [S40, S99]
